title: Question Tags
description: Master question tags for Grade 10 (CBSE/ICSE): the positive-negative rule, helping-verb matching, and special cases (I am, Let's, imperatives, nobody) — bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: The Basic Rule
topics.concept:
Three steps build any tag:

  1. Polarity: a positive statement takes a negative tag; a negative statement takes a positive tag.
  2. Auxiliary: the tag uses the statement's helping verb. If there is no auxiliary, use do/does/did.
    She sings well, doesn't she? They played, didn't they?
  3. Pronoun: the tag's subject is a pronoun matching the statement's subject (Ravi → he, the boys → they, this → it).

The tag is contracted in the negative: is not → isn't, will not → won't, cannot → can't.

examples.solution: aren't you? — positive statement, negative tag, same auxiliary 'are'.

examples.problem: Add a tag: He doesn't like tea, ___?

recap: Positive statement → negative tag; negative → positive
Copy the auxiliary (or use do/does/did if none)
Use a pronoun matching the subject

topics.title: Special Cases
topics.concept:
Some sentences have fixed or tricky tags:

StatementTag
I am late,aren't I?
Let's go,shall we?
Open the door, (command)will you? / won't you?
Don't go,will you?
Everyone is here,aren't they?
Nobody came,did they?
Nothing happened,did it?
This is yours,isn't it?

Watch the hidden negatives: words like never, hardly, scarcely, seldom, nobody, nothing, no one make a statement negative, so they take a positive tag — He never calls, does he?

examples.problem: Add a tag: He hardly ever smiles, ___?
examples.solution: does he? — 'hardly' makes it negative, so the tag is positive.

recap: I am → aren't I; Let's → shall we; imperative → will you/won't you
never/hardly/seldom make the statement negative → positive tag

questions.q: Add the tag: 'You'd rather stay home, ___?'
Choose the correct tag: 'There is little hope, ___?'
questions.explanation: 'little' is a hidden negative → positive tag; subject is 'there'.

questions.q: Add the tag: 'Neither of them agreed, ___?'
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is negative → positive tag, conventionally 'did they?'.

questions.q: Spot the error: 'He used to live here, didn't he?'
Add the tag: 'Let me help you, ___?'
Add the tag: 'I think he is right, ___?'
questions.explanation: With 'I think + clause', the tag agrees with the inner clause: 'isn't he?'.

outcomes: Add the correct question tag to any statement
Match the tag's auxiliary and pronoun to the statement
Handle special cases (I am, Let's, imperatives)

intro.en: A question tag is the short question added at the end of a statement to confirm it: "You're coming, aren't you?" The rules are mechanical and reliable once learned: a positive statement takes a negative tag and vice versa, and the tag copies the statement's helping verb and subject pronoun.
intro.hi: प्रश्न-पुच्छ (question tag) कथन के अंत में जोड़ा गया छोटा प्रश्न है जो उसकी पुष्टि करता है: "You're coming, aren't you?" नियम सीख लेने पर यांत्रिक और भरोसेमंद हैं: सकारात्मक कथन नकारात्मक tag लेता है और इसके उलट, तथा tag कथन की helping verb और subject pronoun की नकल करता है।

real_life.situation:
Everyday confirmations:

You: It's a lovely day, isn't it? You finished the project, didn't you? Let's go out, shall we?
real_life.why: Each tag flips the polarity and copies the right helper: 'is' → 'isn't', 'finished' → 'didn't', and the special 'Let's' → 'shall we'. We use tags constantly in speech — and the board tests them precisely.

rule_box.formula: Positive ↔ negative · copy the auxiliary + subject pronoun
rule_box.example: She can swim, can't she? They don't know, do they?

quick_test.explanation: A positive statement is followed by a negative question tag.

common_mistakes.note: The fixed tag for 'I am' is 'aren't I'.

rearrangement.answer: She is a nurse, isn't she?

reading.passage: "It's a beautiful morning, isn't it?" said Meera. "Let's go for a walk, shall we?" Her brother nodded. "You haven't seen the new park, have you? Nobody told you about it, did they? Come on — you'll love it, won't you?" And so they set out, the dog following them, didn't it?

questions.q: Why is the tag for 'It's a beautiful morning' negative?
questions.answer: The statement is positive, so the tag is negative: 'isn't it?'

questions.q: Explain the tag in 'Nobody told you about it, did they?'
questions.answer: 'Nobody' is a hidden negative, so the tag is positive ('did'), with 'they' for 'nobody'.

questions.q: What tag does 'Let's go for a walk' take and why?
questions.answer: 'shall we?' — the fixed tag for sentences beginning with 'Let's'.

speaking: You're coming with us, aren't you?

writing.prompt: Write five statements about your day, each followed by the correct question tag — include one 'I am…', one 'Let's…' and one with a hidden negative.
writing.example: I am early, aren't I? Let's revise, shall we? You never miss class, do you?

challenge.q: Add the tag: 'Everyone enjoyed the trip, ___?'

challenge.explanation: 'Nothing' is negative → positive tag, subject 'it': 'was it?'.

challenge.q: Add the tag: 'You'd better leave now, ___?'
